chunks: What Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ismaʿil ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

The mukārī, if he does not remain settled in his residence except for five days or less, shortens in his travel by day, completes the night prayer, and the fast of the month of Ramadan is incumbent upon him. But if he has a stay in the town to which he goes for ten days or more, he shortens during his travel and breaks the fast.

key_terms.أَفْطَرَ: he broke the fast, meaning he did not observe the fast due to travel
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: a hired transporter or one whose work involves repeated travel
key_terms.صَوْمُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the obligatory fasting of the month of Ramadan
key_terms.قَصَّرَ: he shortened the four-unit salat (prayer) in travel
key_terms.مُقَامٌ: a period of stay or residence in a place

ai.seo_question: What are the travel prayer and fasting rulings for the mukārī in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the mukārī and how the length of his stay affects salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting) while traveling. It distinguishes between shorter residence periods and a stay of ten days or more, with corresponding rulings on shortening prayer and breaking or observing the fast.
